difficultyReason: Transparent modus ponens structure. Stimulus presents a simple conditional (If A then B), affirms the antecedent, and draws the conclusion. The correct answer uses the identical logical form with entirely different subject matter.
stimulus: If the shipment arrives on time, the warehouse will be fully stocked. The shipment has arrived on time. Therefore, the warehouse is fully stocked.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a musician practices daily, she will master her instrument. Sarah practices daily. Therefore, Sarah will master her instrument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most professional athletes train extensively. James is a professional athlete. Therefore, James probably trains extensively.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the contract is signed, the merger will proceed. The merger did not proceed. Therefore, the contract was not signed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the defendant is guilty or the evidence is unreliable. The evidence is reliable. Therefore, the defendant must be guilty.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All plants require sunlight to grow. This organism grows without sunlight. Therefore, this organism is not a plant.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and A follow modus ponens: If P then Q; P is true; therefore Q is true. The conditional structure and affirmation of the antecedent are identical, only subject matter differs.
explanations.B: Uses probabilistic reasoning ('probably') rather than the definitive conditional chain of the stimulus.
explanations.C: Uses modus tollens (conditional + denial of consequent) rather than modus ponens.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism, not conditional reasoning.
explanations.E: Uses categorical logic and contrapositive, not the simple conditional affirmation of the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Clear disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. The stimulus presents an explicit disjunction, denies one disjunct, and concludes the other. Answer choices mix conditional chains, universals, and other forms to test whether students can isolate the disjunctive structure.
stimulus: Either the report was completed yesterday or it will be completed tomorrow. The report was not completed yesterday. Therefore, the report will be completed tomorrow.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All birds have feathers. This creature has feathers. Therefore, this creature is a bird.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If inflation rises, the central bank will raise interest rates. Inflation has risen. Therefore, the central bank will raise interest rates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the suspect fled the country or is hiding locally. The suspect did not flee the country. Therefore, the suspect is hiding locally.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most employees arrive before nine o'clock. This employee arrives before nine o'clock. Therefore, most employees is a reasonable generalization.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the patient has the virus, she will show symptoms. The patient does not show symptoms. Therefore, the patient does not have the virus.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and C follow disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. The structure of disjunction + denial + remaining conclusion is identical.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent (invalid form), not a valid disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.B: Uses modus ponens (conditional + affirmation), not disjunction.
explanations.D: Inductive generalization, not a deductive disjunctive form.
explanations.E: Uses modus tollens (conditional + denial of consequent), not disjunction.

difficultyReason: Simple contrapositive (modus tollens) form: If A then B; not B; therefore not A. The structure is transparent — students must recognize that denying the consequent allows us to deny the antecedent. Distractors use modus ponens, affirm consequent, or categorical logic.
stimulus: If a restaurant has poor sanitation, it will fail the health inspection. The restaurant did not fail the health inspection. Therefore, the restaurant does not have poor sanitation.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a student studies hard, they will pass the exam. This student studied hard. Therefore, this student will pass the exam.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a contract is breached, the other party can sue. The other party did not sue. Therefore, the contract was not breached.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All successful entrepreneurs take risks. These entrepreneurs are successful. Therefore, these entrepreneurs take risks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the supplier is reliable or the delivery is late. The delivery is not late. Therefore, the supplier is reliable.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most companies invest in research. This company invests in research. Therefore, this company is probably successful.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow modus tollens: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. The denial of the consequent leads to denial of the antecedent in both.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens (affirms antecedent), not modus tollens.
explanations.C: Uses categorical logic (universal + particular), not a conditional chain.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism, not a conditional denial.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic language.

difficultyReason: Conditional chain (hypothetical syllogism): If A then B; if B then C; A is true; therefore C. Students must track the transitive property through two conditionals and an initial premise. Distractors offer single conditionals, invalid chains, or categorical universals.
stimulus: If the regulatory approval is obtained, the project will be funded. If the project is funded, construction will begin. Regulatory approval has been obtained. Therefore, construction will begin.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the economy is strong, consumers spend more. Consumers are spending more. Therefore, the economy is strong.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a drug is approved for use, doctors will prescribe it. If doctors prescribe it, patients will take it. The drug is approved. Therefore, patients will take it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All mammals breathe oxygen. This animal breathes oxygen. Therefore, this animal is a mammal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the bill passes or the provision is abandoned. The bill did not pass. Therefore, the provision is abandoned.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most people who exercise regularly are healthy. Marcus exercises regularly. Therefore, Marcus is probably healthy.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B use hypothetical syllogism: If P then Q; If Q then R; P; therefore R. The chain of two conditionals plus affirmation of the starting premise matches exactly.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens with affirmation of consequent (invalid).
explanations.C: Uses categorical universal logic, not chained conditionals.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probability markers.

difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular instantiation: All A are B; X is A; therefore X is B. This is among the simplest deductive forms. Distractors confuse this with converses, probabilistic inferences, disjunctions, or conditional chains.
stimulus: All members of the committee must sign the agreement. Jordan is a member of the committee. Therefore, Jordan must sign the agreement.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If someone is a manager, they have supervisory responsibilities. Kim has supervisory responsibilities. Therefore, Kim is a manager.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every student enrolled in this course must attend at least one seminar. Elena is enrolled in this course. Therefore, Elena must attend at least one seminar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the meeting will be rescheduled or the attendees will be notified. The attendees will not be notified. Therefore, the meeting will be rescheduled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some critics of the proposal are economists. This person is a critic of the proposal. Therefore, this person is probably an economist.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the merger succeeds, the two companies will consolidate. The merger has succeeded. Therefore, the companies will consolidate.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow universal instantiation: All/Every A must be B; X is A; therefore X must be B. The structure of universal claim + particular case + necessary conclusion is identical.
explanations.A: Affirms consequent (invalid), not a universal instantiation.
explanations.D: Uses inductive reasoning with a probabilistic ('probably') qualifier.

difficultyReason: Simple analogy with parallel structure: X and Y share properties P and Q; Y has property R; therefore X has property R. The conclusion transfers a property across a likeness. Distractors use conditionals, universals, or failed analogies.
stimulus: Orchestral music and chamber music both use multiple instrumental voices and follow classical forms. Chamber music creates an intimate listening experience. Therefore, orchestral music also creates an intimate listening experience.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a team has strong coaching, it will win championships. This team has strong coaching. Therefore, this team will win championships.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All professional athletes dedicate themselves to their sport. This person is a professional athlete. Therefore, this person dedicates themselves to their sport.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Novels and short stories both employ narrative structure and character development. Novels are commercially published. Therefore, short stories are commercially published.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the defendant acted with intent or acted recklessly. The defendant did not act with intent. Therefore, the defendant acted recklessly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If deforestation accelerates, endangered species will disappear. Deforestation has accelerated. Therefore, endangered species will disappear.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and C follow analogical reasoning: X and Y share P and Q; Y has R; therefore X has R. The parallel structure transfers a property based on noted similarities.

difficultyReason: Modus ponens with a real-world policy context: If condition P holds, outcome Q follows; P holds; therefore Q. The structure is transparent, and distractors use different logical forms or the wrong direction in conditionals.
stimulus: If unemployment rises above five percent, the government must increase job training programs. Unemployment has risen above five percent. Therefore, the government must increase job training programs.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a company pollutes local water sources, it will face legal penalties. This company has faced legal penalties. Therefore, this company pollutes local water sources.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a species loses its habitat, it is at risk of extinction. This species has lost its habitat. Therefore, this species is at risk of extinction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the new policy is beneficial or it is harmful. The policy is not harmful. Therefore, the policy is beneficial.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All environmental regulations protect public health. This regulation protects public health. Therefore, this regulation is environmental.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most candidates with relevant experience are hired for the position. This candidate has relevant experience. Therefore, this candidate is probably hired.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow modus ponens: If P then Q; P is true; therefore Q is true. The conditional structure and affirmation of the antecedent match.
explanations.A: Affirms consequent (invalid), reversing the conditional direction.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic qualifier.

difficultyReason: Two-premise modus tollens in an economic context: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. The denial of the consequent triggers denial of the antecedent. Distractors offer affirming consequent, modus ponens, or categorical forms.
stimulus: If a company reduces operating costs, it will increase profitability. This company did not increase profitability. Therefore, this company did not reduce operating costs.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If attendance drops below minimum, the event will be canceled. Attendance has dropped below minimum. Therefore, the event will be canceled.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All efficient supply chains reduce delivery delays. This supply chain reduces delivery delays. Therefore, this supply chain is efficient.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a student submits work late, the grade will be reduced. This student's grade was not reduced. Therefore, this student did not submit work late.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the contract is legally binding or it contains ambiguities. The contract does not contain ambiguities. Therefore, the contract is legally binding.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most companies that invest in technology see growth. This company sees growth. Therefore, this company probably invests in technology.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and C follow modus tollens: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Denying the consequent permits denying the antecedent in identical form.

difficultyReason: Three-premise conditional chain in a medical context: If A then B; If B then C; A is true; therefore C. The chain is straightforward, and distractors include failed chains, single conditionals, or non-conditional forms.
stimulus: If a patient has high blood pressure, medication will be prescribed. If medication is prescribed, regular monitoring will be required. This patient has high blood pressure. Therefore, regular monitoring will be required.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a witness is credible, the testimony is admissible. The testimony is admissible. Therefore, the witness is credible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a forest fire spreads to populated areas, evacuation orders will be issued. If evacuation orders are issued, residents must leave. A forest fire has spread to populated areas. Therefore, residents must leave.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All licensed therapists follow ethical guidelines. This person follows ethical guidelines. Therefore, this person is a licensed therapist.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the diagnosis is correct or the patient will need further tests. The diagnosis is correct. Therefore, the patient will not need further tests.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most people with seasonal allergies take antihistamines. Marcus takes antihistamines. Therefore, Marcus probably has seasonal allergies.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow hypothetical syllogism with three components: If P then Q; If Q then R; P; therefore R. The transitive chain through two conditionals matches.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens with affirmation of consequent (invalid).
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism with a flawed conclusion structure.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic reasoning.

difficultyReason: Universal categorical with negative instantiation: All A are B; X is not B; therefore X is not A. This follows the contrapositive of categorical logic and mirrors the logical form of modus tollens. Distractors offer affirmations, valid but non-parallel forms, or inductive reasoning.
stimulus: All candidates who pass the bar exam will be licensed to practice law. This graduate did not become licensed to practice law. Therefore, this graduate did not pass the bar exam.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic language.
